rationale: The low score reflects what automation cannot check, not a defect in the change. The four unmeasured items are limits of the pass, stated in the gate evidence rather than hidden: it drives Chrome only, does not test screen-reader output, cannot tell whether a copy is clear to a first-time reader, and the ported code was written against a base roughly 50 commits behind main. Only loading the page in a browser revealed the render failure, which is the argument for accepting the browser pass as sufficient evidence here. A cross-feature collection collision with WF-045 was also caught and resolved before landing. This override accepts the residual risk of an unexercised second browser and no assistive-technology testing, on the basis that the change is a recovered port whose behaviour is covered by 288 of its own tests and whose accessibility has been measured on every tab at every breakpoint.
closes: Firefox and Safari are not exercised by the browser pass, and screen-reader announcements are not verified. Neither is claimed as done. The next workflow that touches a shared primitive should extend tools/design_floor_browser.py to a second browser engine before its own landing, so the gap closes once rather than per feature.
